title: More Than 129 Missing After Indonesian Ferry Overturns in Java Sea
excerpt: The Virgo Transport 8, carrying 243 people from Surabaya to Banjarmasin, capsized in rough seas early Sunday. Rescuers have saved 108 people and recovered six bodies as a dozen vessels and two helicopters comb the Java Sea.
body:
• At least 129 people were missing after the passenger ferry Virgo Transport 8 overturned in the Java Sea in bad weather early Sunday.
  • At least 108 people were rescued and the bodies of six passengers were recovered as the search expanded around the vessel's last known position.
  • The ferry was carrying 243 people — 213 passengers and 30 crew — from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan.
  • The captain reported rough seas with waves up to 3 meters (10 feet) and issued a distress call saying the ship was listing before contact was lost at about 2 a.m.

Rescue teams are searching the Java Sea for at least 129 people still missing after a passenger ferry overturned in rough seas early Sunday, in an accident that has mobilized a dozen vessels — including four navy ships — and two helicopters.

The Virgo Transport 8 was traveling from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan province on Borneo island when the captain reported rough seas with waves up to 3 meters (10 feet) before issuing a distress call saying the ship was listing, said I Putu Sudayana, who heads the Banjarmasin Search and Rescue Office. Authorities later received information indicating the vessel had overturned.

Contact with the vessel was lost at about 2 a.m. Sunday, and the rescue agency in Banjarmasin said it received a report two hours later. By Sunday afternoon, rescue teams backed by a dozen vessels — four of them navy ships — and two helicopters were converging on the ferry's last known position, about 148 kilometers (92 miles) from a pier in Banjarmasin. An aerial image released by Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency (BASARNAS) showed the upturned hull of the Virgo Transport 8 above the waterline.

Context & Background

The ship's manifest listed 243 people on board — 213 passengers and 30 crew members — though the Associated Press reported it is common in Indonesia for actual passenger numbers to differ from the manifest. Surabaya, Indonesia's second-largest city, sits across the Java Sea from Banjarmasin, a port city on the island of Borneo, making the crossing one of the country's busiest inter-island passenger routes.

"The ship's operator reported the incident to authorities after receiving information that the vessel had encountered bad weather."

— I Putu Sudayana, head of the Banjarmasin Search and Rescue Office

Impact & Analysis

The figures account for every name on the manifest: 129 people missing, 108 rescued and six bodies recovered add up to the 243 listed aboard, leaving rescue coordinators with a precise — and daunting — list of the unaccounted. The scale of the response, with the navy committing four ships to the civilian-led operation alongside helicopters sweeping the Java Sea, reflects how seriously Indonesian authorities are treating the disaster.

The captain's final reports — three-meter waves, a listing hull, then silence — suggest the ship ran into trouble quickly in heavy seas, though officials have not yet said what caused the ferry to overturn. Sudayana told reporters in a video briefing that the vessel's operator alerted authorities only after learning the ship had encountered the bad weather, raising questions about the timeline between the distress call and the start of the search.

What's Next

The search was continuing around the vessel's last known position, with authorities widening the search area as additional assets arrived on scene. Officials had not released a revised casualty count beyond the 108 rescued and six bodies recovered. With the upturned hull located, attention will turn to recovering the vessel and establishing why a fully loaded passenger ferry capsized on a routine crossing.
